title: Private deployments: breakeven & sensitivity playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook and lightweight spreadsheet narrative to help product + solutions quickly estimate on-prem vs VPC breakeven and run sensitivity experiments for licensing + support bundles. It's intentionally informal: use this to populate the canonical spreadsheet (TODO below).

Summary / TL;DR:
- High-level formula: Annualized on-prem cost = (HW_capex + infra_setup + network_setup)/amort_years + annual_ops + recurring_support + electricity + datacenter_rent + personnel_alloc. VPC cost = cloud_infra_run_rate + network_egress + managed_service_fee + support.
- Typical break-even horizon: 18-36 months depending on utilization and GPU pricing. For 24/7 high-utilization workloads (>70% GPU hours) on-prem often breaks even; for spiky workloads VPC usually wins.
- Licensing + support bundles materially change the economics: a high-touch "Premium" support at +35-50% can tilt customers to VPC even if raw infra is cheaper on-prem.

Key assumptions (use these baseline numbers in the spreadsheet cells):
- HW: A100 80GB equivalent per node list price (2025 baseline): $35,000. Use 3-year amortization by default.
- Rack + networking + storage per node (CAPEX): $10,000.
- Integration/setup one-time services: $40k for first datacenter (distributed across customers in model if we sell as turn-key).
- Annual ops (maintenance, spare parts, KVM, remote hands): 8% of HW CAPEX (~$3k per GPU node).
- Power & cooling: $2k-$6k per GPU node/year depending on PUE and region.
- SRE/ops FTE time allocation: 0.1-0.5 FTE per 8-GPU cluster depending on automation maturity (use $180k fully burdened salary).
- Cloud/VPC equivalent: GPU hour price (on-demand baseline) $4.50/hour for high-memory instances; reserved / committed discounts up to 50%. Include network egress $0.02/GB.

Model components to include as separate rows in the sheet (explicit):
- CAPEX: HW_purchase, racks, switch, storage arrays, deployment services.
- CAPEX amortization period (years).
- One-time migration/validation professional services.
- OPEX recurring: power, cooling, network colo, monitoring, backups, license renewals.
- Personnel: SRE, infra, security per-customer allocation.
- Licensing: model-serving runtime license per node or per vCPU, 3 pricing patterns (per-node flat, per-concurrent-req, per-token).
- Support: Bronze/Standard/Premium with defined SLAs and included hours.
- Opportunity cost / capital: company WACC or customer discount rate to annualize capex (5-12%).

Scenario examples (cells to build):
- Small proof-of-concept: 2 GPU nodes, 40% utilization, 36 month horizon => VPC favored.
- Mid: 8 GPU nodes, 60% utilization, 24 month horizon => ambiguous, licensing/support matters.
- Large enterprise: 64 GPU nodes, 80% utilization, 24 month horizon => on-prem likely wins if support <= 30% of recurring costs.

Break-even heuristic (quick math you can write into the spreadsheet):
- Breakeven_months = (One_time_onprem_cost + (annual_onprem - annual_vpc) * (months/12) ) solve for months where cumulative cost equal. Simpler: Monthly_onprem = (capex/amort_months) + monthly_opex + monthly_support; Monthly_vpc = cloud_hour_rate * reserved_hours_per_month + cloud_network + managed_fee. Solve Monthly_onprem = Monthly_vpc for target months given amortization.

Sensitivity buckets to include (create slider inputs in sheet):
- GPU list price +/- 30%
- Utilization +/- 30ppt
- Electricity cost +/- 50%
- Support premium multiplier (1.0/1.35/1.5)
- Amortization 2-5 years

Licensing + support bundle suggestions (bundle names, inclusion, and suggested markup):
- Standard: runtime license per-node annual $6k, email support, 72-hr SLA for critical. Suggested markup: 20% margin.
- Enterprise: $12k/node/year, phone + 24/7 incident support, 24-hr response for P1, includes basic onboarding credits (40 hours). Suggested markup: 25-35% margin.
- Premium: $20k/node/year or custom % of invoice, white-glove onboarding (200 hours), SLA 4-hr P1, dedicated solutions engineer and quarterly review. Suggested markup: 35-50% margin.
- Add-ons: Security hardening (per engagement), SOC2/AZURE/GCP marketplace packaging fee, extended retention for telemetry. Price per add-on in spreadsheet.

Optimization levers (recommendations we can present to customers to reduce TCO):
1) Quantization + mixed precision to reduce memory footprint enabling cheaper GPU types.
2) Model distillation / smaller ensembles to reduce per-token compute.
3) Workload multiplexing (consolidate low latency + batch) to increase utilization.
4) Autoscaling with fast cold-start strategies and lightweight hot-cache nodes for burst.
5) Prefix/KV caching for session-heavy chat use-cases.
6) Hybrid routing: Keep latency-critical traffic on dedicated or hosted, move batch/retries to cheaper private clusters.
7) Runbook + run-rate SLOs to minimize SRE FTEs over time.

Pricing sensitivity insight (guidance text we use in presales):
- "If the customer's steady-state utilization is >65% and they plan 24-months+ of committed usage, propose on-prem with an Enterprise support bundle. For irregular/spiky workloads with <40% baseline utilization, recommend VPC + Reserved capacity for sporadic commit."

Customer-facing selling points to include in proposal templates (short bullets):
- Predictable unit economics with on-prem: lock hardware pricing and avoid egress surprises.
- Rapid support escalation options and white-glove onboarding reduce migration time and risk.
- Hybrid mode for staged migration: start with VPC + data sync to private deployment to reduce cutover risk.

Open questions / TODOs (things to finalize in canonical spreadsheet):
- Finalize per-node list price for 2025 contract rates (ask procurement for discounts).
- Add region-specific PUE and power rates (US-West / EU / APAC).
- Create dedicated sheet to model licensing per-concurrent-request pricing.
- Build a sensitivity dashboard and export screenshots for sales playbook.
- Run 5 customer case studies for different scales and populate template.

Immediate next steps (action items):
- [Priya] Draft canonical spreadsheet using baseline cells above (due 2025-02-09).
- [Marcus] Pull procurement price list and typical partner discounts (due 2025-01-22).
- [Arielle] Create sensitivity dashboard prototype in Looker/Sheets and add to sales assets (due 2025-02-15).
- Create GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deployments/issues/84 to track spreadsheet canonicalization.

Notes / rough heuristics to surface during sales call:
- "We assume 3-year amortization by default; if customer wants 5 years, show revised breakeven and flag hardware warranty and EOL risk."
- "Support costs are directional: for initial sizing show Standard and Enterprise only; Premium is for strategic deals where success engineering is required."

Appendix: formula cheat-sheet to copy into sheet cells (human-friendly):
- annualized_capex = (hw_cost + infra_cost + setup_cost) / amort_years
- annual_onprem_total = annualized_capex + annual_ops + annual_support + annual_power + personnel_alloc + misc
- monthly_vpc = instance_hour_price * hours_per_month * (1 - reserved_discount) + network_egress + managed_service_fee
- breakeven_months = (one_time_onprem + monthly_onprem_diff_positive * amort_months) / monthly_vpc_diff (leave to sheet solver)

Quick reference: sample numbers (do not present as final):
- 8x-A100 cluster (capex hw): $280k, rack+nw: $40k, setup: $40k, amort 3y => monthly capex = $9.4k. annual_opex ~ $20k, support enterprise $96k/yr => monthly_onprem_total ~ $20k. VPC equivalent (reserved) ~ $18k/mo. Close call; licensing/support flips.

End of draft playbook. Keep this doc as the presales narrative for the canonical sheet. If you edit numbers here, update linked GH issue and the spreadsheet export.
